item.title: Community Briefs 2/12/26
item.description: Archbald Winter Carnival, kickoff of borough’s 150th birthday celebration, rescheduled Archbald will kick off its 150th birthday celebrations with a winter carnival Saturday. The event, originally scheduled for Feb. 7, was rescheduled to Feb. 14 due to a forecast of inclement weather and frigid temperatures, according to the Archbald Neighborhood Association Facebook page. item.title: Beautiful Blocks program accepting applications
item.description: Applications are now being accepted for this year's Beautiful Blocks home improvement program. Beautiful Blocks is jointly sponsored by NeighborWorks Northeastern Pennsylvania and the cities of Carbondale, Scranton and Pittston.

item.title: Why the Y: Why being a Y day camp counselor is the summer job you’ll never forget
item.description: If you’re looking for a summer job that’s more than a paycheck, you’ll find it at the Greater Scranton YMCA. As a day camp counselor, you’ll make a real difference in kids’ lives and have fun every single day.

item.title: Carbondale Area FBLA members compete in Regional Leadership Conference
item.description: Carbondale Area Junior/Senior High School Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA) competed Jan. 9 at the Regional Leadership Conference at the University of Scranton.

item.title: Snapshots: Scenes from Jessup Groundhog Day
item.description: Hundreds gathered at Station Park for the inaugural Jessup Groundhog Day celebration on Feb. 1 to watch Jessup Giuseppe, a weather-prognosticating ferret, make his prediction. The ferret chose a white grape, signifying an early spring. Here are some scenes from the crowd that gathered for the event.

item.title: ‘Springtime is near’: Jessup Giuseppe the ferret predicts early spring at inaugural event
item.description: Hundreds gathered at Station Park for the inaugural Jessup Groundhog Day celebration on Feb. 1 to watch Jessup Giuseppe, a weather-prognosticating ferret, make his prediction. The ferret, belonging to James “Jessup Jim” Salus, chose a white grape, signifying an early spring and winning over the bundled-up crowd. item.title: LOCAL COLLEGE: Scranton men stage another big comeback win
item.description: The University of Scranton men’s basketball team is becoming the cardiac comeback kids. For the second consecutive Wednesday, the Royals overcame a double-digit halftime deficit to edge Lycoming College, 70-69, in a Landmark Conference game at Lamade Gymnasium in Williamsport. Last week, Scranton trailed Moravian by as many as 19 points in the first half and by 16 at halftime, but rallied for an 84-80 win.
